findings.description: The security group allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressed instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the host.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 serving cleartext HTTP, and egress is unrestricted to all ports/protocols/destinations, which permits data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic from a compromised instance.

findings.issue_category: hard-coded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable by any process or attacker on the instance via the metadata service (169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) and is stored unencrypted in the instance description.

No metadata_options block enforces http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with a public-facing web server, this allows SSRF against the application to retrieve instance metadata and credentials.
The instance defines no root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume storing the OS and any application data is unencrypted at rest.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a default route to the internet gateway, placing it directly on the public internet with no load balancer, NAT, or bastion boundary in front of it.
The EBS data volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk, so a copy of the volume data persists unencrypted and can be shared or restored without key controls.

The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (SSE-KMS or SSE-S3), so network telemetry that reveals internal topology and traffic patterns is stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy restricts this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose flow log data publicly without any account-level guardrail.
The bucket has no policy denying non-HTTPS requests (aws:SecureTransport false), permitting cleartext retrieval of stored flow log data.

findings.issue_category: force destroy on audit log store
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the flow log bucket and all retained network audit records to be deleted in a single destroy operation, undermining log integrity and tamper resistance.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP automatically, defeating network segmentation and exposing workloads directly to the internet by default.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes this subnet public by default, so any future instance placed here is automatically internet-reachable via the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway.
The VPC's implicit default security group is not locked down via aws_default_security_group, leaving a group that permits all intra-group traffic available for attachment to future resources.
